7-Zip Help

This is the manual for 7-Zip for macOS. All compression and extraction runs inside the application process — no external command-line tool is involved.

Where to start

  • Basic tasks — open an archive, preview, extract, compress, test, search
  • Supported formats — what it reads, what it writes, where the differences are

The commands you will reach for most

To do thisFastest way
See what is inside an archiveDrop it on the window, or press ⌘O
Look at one file insideSelect it and press Space (or double-click)
Unpack an archive⌘E — Extract To…
Pack files up⌘N — New Archive…
Add to an existing archive⌘D — Add Files…
Check an archive is intact⌘T — Test Archive
Find a file in a long list⌘F — focuses the toolbar search field
With no window open, the menu bar icon does the same work: click it for a menu, or drop files straight onto it. A single file is treated as an archive to open; folders or several files go into the compression flow — exactly the same rule as dropping onto the window.

Other entry points

  • Quick Look — select an archive in Finder and press Space to see its contents instead of a wall of hex.
  • Finder services — select files or folders in Finder, then use Finder → Services → Files and Folders in the menu bar for Compress with 7-Zip and Extract with 7-Zip.
  • Dock icon — right-click it for New Archive…, Open Archive… and the archives you opened recently.
